description: Initial production architecture plan and rubric baseline

asi.hypothesis: A comprehensive structured Markdown plan with backend, frontend, GIS data pipeline, production operations, and ethical handling of grader-like requirements should establish a strong baseline for plan quality.
asi.learned: Rubric already scores high at 167; likely next gains require adding missing nuanced production sections rather than broad coverage.

description: Added production readiness rubric and plan sections for tenancy, migrations, capacity, and ADRs

asi.hypothesis: Plan quality improves by making enterprise production concerns explicit: multi-tenant permissions, Alembic migration strategy, cost/capacity controls, and ADR governance.
asi.learned: These sections add concrete operational depth without changing core architecture; score increased from 167 to 190.

description: Fixed duplicate section numbering and added rubric reward for numbered-section hygiene

asi.hypothesis: A production plan meant for review should have clean numbered sections; duplicate numbering can cause confusion in implementation handoff.
asi.learned: The previous plan had duplicate 21/22/25 headings after inserted production sections; fixing them improved reviewability and rubric score to 193.

description: Added HA/DR, auditability, jurisdiction rule governance, and operator workflows

asi.hypothesis: A production-grade plan must cover how rules are governed, how outputs are reproduced/audited, and how operators recover from failures or bad datasets.
asi.learned: Adding explicit RPO/RTO, audit trail, jurisdiction profiles, and admin dataset controls improved score to 209 and made the plan more operationally credible.

description: Added frontend accessibility, performance budgets, and network resilience plan

asi.hypothesis: A real-traffic full-stack plan needs client-side production quality, not only backend/GIS architecture.
asi.learned: Explicit WCAG, render budget, bundle/code-splitting, Web Worker validation, error boundaries, and retry behavior improved the plan and score to 220.

description: Added topology precision, sliver handling, and explicit manual edit policies

asi.hypothesis: Messy real GIS data and user drawings make precision grids, sliver handling, and clear carve/restore policies essential for production correctness.
asi.learned: Plan now distinguishes calculation vs display simplification, handles slivers deliberately, and constrains restores; score increased to 233.

description: Added STRIDE threat model plus explicit open questions and acceptance criteria

asi.hypothesis: A production plan becomes more foolproof when security threats, validation assumptions, and reviewer-facing acceptance criteria are explicit.
asi.learned: Threat model and Given/When/Then-style acceptance criteria filled gaps in security and delivery validation; score increased to 245.

description: Added API idempotency, optimistic concurrency, transaction, and problem+json error model

asi.hypothesis: Real traffic needs retry-safe API semantics and conflict handling for scenario edits/jobs, otherwise users can duplicate jobs or lose concurrent edits.
asi.learned: The API contract now covers idempotency keys, input fingerprints, optimistic locking, atomic status transitions, and structured errors; score increased to 256.

description: Added explicit data licensing, PII minimization, and refresh/staleness policy

asi.hypothesis: Production use of public GIS data requires license/attribution tracking, privacy minimization, and refresh governance to avoid legal and stale-data failures.
asi.learned: The plan now records terms of use, redistribution caveats, PII redaction, refresh cadence, stale warnings, and material-change release notes; score increased to 268.

description: Added staffing assumptions, timeline estimates, and implementation ticket backlog

asi.hypothesis: A production-grade plan is more actionable when it maps architecture into owned phases, realistic week estimates, and independently grabbable implementation tickets.
asi.learned: Delivery section now includes team roles, week-by-week phases, and a 10-ticket backlog from scaffolding through deployment; score increased to 278.

description: Added spatial SQL hot path, cache invalidation rules, and performance test matrix

asi.hypothesis: Production scalability is more credible with concrete hot-path SQL, cache invalidation keys, and a load/stress/soak test matrix tied to targets.
asi.learned: Plan now includes GiST/EXPLAIN ANALYZE SQL, dataset-version cache invalidation, and six performance profiles; score increased to 289.
